data.title: Delhi HC enforces BharatPe's shareholder-agreement veto over Unity Bank's capital change
data.summary: A Delhi High Court division bench dismissed Unity Small Finance Bank's appeal and kept in place an order stopping it from putting a plan to raise its authorised share capital before its board without the written consent of BharatPe's parent, Resilient Innovations, as their shareholders' agreement requires. A consent right written into a shareholders' agreement can be enforced by a court, so negotiate these 'reserved matters' carefully before you sign.

src.t: LiveLaw Business: Delhi High Court rejects Unity Small Finance Bank plea (Unity Small Finance Bank v Resilient Innovations, FAO(OS)(COMM) 221/2026), 9 Nov 2026

data.plain: The most share value a company is allowed to issue, as written in its founding documents. To issue more shares beyond it, the company must first formally raise this limit.
